t:
Section 2612 of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 300ff–22) is amended—

    (1) by striking “A State may use” and inserting “(a) In General.—A State may use”; and 
    (2) by adding at the end the following subsections:
“(b) Support Services; Outreach.—The purposes for which a grant under this part may be used include delivering or enhancing the following:
“(1) Outpatient and ambulatory support services under section 2611(a) (including case management) to the extent that such services facilitate, enhance, support, or sustain the delivery, continuity, or benefits of health services for individuals and families with HIV disease.
“(2) Outreach activities that are intended to identify individuals with HIV disease who know their HIV status and are not receiving HIV-related services, and that are—
“(A) necessary to implement the strategy under section 2617(b)(4)(B), including activities facilitating the access of such individuals to HIV-related primary care services at entities described in subsection (c)(1);
“(B) conducted in a manner consistent with the requirement under section 2617(b)(6)(G) and 2651(b)(2); and
“(C) supplement, and do not supplant, such activities that are carried out with amounts appropriated under section 317.
“(c) Early Intervention Services.—
“(1) In general.—The purposes for which a grant under this part may be used include providing to individuals with HIV disease early intervention services described in section 2651(b)(2), with follow-up referral provided for the purpose of facilitating the access of individuals receiving the services to HIV-related health services. The entities through which such services may be provided under the grant include public health departments, emergency rooms, substance abuse and mental health treatment programs, detoxification centers, detention facilities, clinics regarding sexually transmitted diseases, homeless shelters, HIV disease counseling and testing sites, health care points of entry specified by States or eligible areas, federally qualified health centers, and entities described in section
2652(a) that constitute a point of access to services by maintaining referral relationships.
“(2) Conditions.—With respect to an entity that proposes to provide early intervention services under paragraph (1), such paragraph applies only if the entity demonstrates to the satisfaction of the State involved that—
“(A) Federal, State, or local funds are otherwise inadequate for the early intervention services the entity proposes to provide; and
“(B) the entity will expend funds pursuant to such paragraph to supplement and not supplant other funds available to the entity for the provision of early intervention services for the fiscal year involved.
“(d) Quality Management.—
“(1) Requirement.—Each State that receives a grant under this part shall provide for the establishment of a quality management program to assess the extent to which HIV health services provided to patients under the grant are consistent with the most recent Public Health Service guidelines for the treatment of HIV disease and related opportunistic infection, and as applicable, to develop strategies for ensuring that such services are consistent with the guidelines for improvement in the access to and quality of HIV health services.
“(2) Use of funds.—From amounts received under a grant awarded under this part for a fiscal year, the State may (in addition to amounts to which section 2618(b)(5) applies) use for activities associated with the quality management program required in paragraph (1) not more than the lesser of—
“(A) 5 percent of amounts received under the grant; or
“(B) $3,000,000.”.

fable.w: The section specifies permissible uses of grant funds by States (support services, outreach, early intervention, quality management) and conditions on sub-entities. The tempting reading is that references to States, public health departments and entities making demonstrations amount to outside involvement, but those are grant-use conditions and a showing made to the State, not to a federal decision-maker. Nothing requires the federal government to consult outsiders, hold hearings, issue rules, form an advisory body, or grant a right to sue.

qwen_block.w: This section outlines the permissible uses of funds for grants awarded to States under the Public Health Service Act. It details requirements for support services, outreach, early intervention, and quality management programs that the grantee (the State) must implement. There is no provision requiring the federal government to consult with or coordinate with outside parties (such as the public, experts, or other governments) before making a decision. The interactions described are between the federal government and the grant recipient (the State) regarding the administration of the grant, which falls under the exclusion for applications/grants and intra-governmental coordination.
qwen_block.s: The purposes for which a grant under this part may be used include delivering or enhancing the following:
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement for a State to establish a "quality management program" or the conditions for entities to demonstrate adequacy of funds implies some form of consultation or participation. However, these are internal administrative requirements for grant recipients (States and local entities) to ensure compliance with federal guidelines. There is no requirement for the federal government to consult with the public, states, or other outside parties *before* making a decision; rather, the States are implementing programs as a condition of receiving funds. The text describes how grant money can be used and what programs must be established by the grantee, not a participatory process involving outsiders in federal decision-making.

opus.w: The section lists the permitted uses of HIV grant funds and requires States that receive grants to set up quality management programs. These are grant-administration provisions, which the definition excludes. The only point where an outside entity interacts with a government is when it shows the State that it qualifies, and that decision is the State's, not a federal one. Nothing here requires a comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, or outside consultation before a federal decision.

opus.b:
**Step 1: The tempting reading and why it fails.** It is tempting to read subsection (c)(2) as participation, because an outside entity must "demonstrate to the satisfaction of the State" before it can provide services. But that decision belongs to the State, not the federal government. The section otherwise only lists what the grant money may be spent on and requires States to run a quality management program. Nothing brings outsiders into a federal decision: there is no comment period, rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue. Using grant funds is a benefit or grant matter, which the definition excludes.

**Step 2: Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section outlines the permissible uses of grant funds and administrative requirements for States receiving those grants. It does not require the federal government to consult with outside parties before making a decision. The 'quality management program' is an internal requirement for the State grantee, not a federal decision-making process involving public participation. The section deals with grant administration and service delivery, which are excluded from the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s:
(d) Quality Management.—
“(1) Requirement.—Each State that receives a grant under this part shall provide for the establishment of a quality management program to assess the extent to which HIV health services provided to patients under the grant are consistent with the most recent Public Health Service guidelines for the treatment of HIV disease and related opportunistic infection, and as applicable, to develop strategies for ensuring that such services are consistent with the guidelines for improvement in the access to and quality of HIV health services.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the requirement for a State to establish a "quality management program" involves participation because it requires assessing services and developing strategies, potentially involving patients or providers. However, the text does not specify that outside parties must be consulted or involved in this assessment; it is an internal administrative requirement for the grant recipient (the State). Furthermore, the section primarily describes how grant funds can be used (outpatient services, outreach, early intervention), which falls under the exclusion for "applications for benefits or grants" or general program administration, not public participation in federal decision-making. The actors involved in the decision-making described (the State, the Secretary) are either the grant recipient or the federal agency, and there is no mechanism for outside public input into the federal decision to award or manage the grant.
